prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal] find hitch cause and fixes
[action] analyzed capture + sensors
[result] wrote result.json
[next] done

Found: every ~4 s the rig drops PCIe to L1 (sensors show L1 entries at seconds 2,6,10,14,...,50, along with RP0/RP1 L1 in BIOS); each L1 event stalls 12-13 frames (~22 ms vs ~6.9 ms baseline), exactly matching the 13-14 clusters seen in the frame log. Defender window at 43-45 s (DPC 420-455 µs, disk ~90%, MsMpEng.exe) produces no present stalls, so it is not the cause. Average 137.29 fps, 1% low 45.35 fps (p99 22.05 ms). Changes: pcie_aspm_rp0_nvme L1→disabled, pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu L1→disabled (link speed Gen5 x4 untouched, no BIOS overclock).

Assumptions: L1→disabled chosen over L0s to be unambiguous; RP2 chipset left as-is.
